answers.answer: The model emits it as an ordinary predicted token. Self-RAG expands the model's vocabulary with reflection tokens and trains the generator on text interleaved with those tokens and retrieved passages, so producing them is next-token prediction. The same forward pass that would write the next span of prose writes the retrieval token instead, and there is no separate classifier or controller in front of the retriever.
accept: the decision is emitted as a predicted token from an expanded vocabulary
it is trained as ordinary next-token prediction
there is no separate classifier or controller component

answers.answer: Retrieving whether or not retrieval is necessary, and retrieving passages whether or not they are relevant. A fixed k is chosen before the question arrives, so nothing in the pipeline can decline to retrieve for a question that needs no passages, and nothing can shrink the set when only some of the 5 are relevant. Self-RAG replaces it with a model that retrieves on demand.
accept: retrieval happens even when it is not necessary
passages are incorporated regardless of relevance
k is fixed before the question, so neither decision has anywhere to be made

answers.answer: The probability of generating the Retrieve=Yes token, normalised over all the output tokens the Retrieve token can take, is compared against the threshold; if it surpasses the bar, retrieval fires. The threshold is set from outside the model rather than learned, so a person picks it. Lowering it lets more steps clear the bar, so the system retrieves more often.
accept: the normalised probability of the Retrieve=Yes token
normalised over the Retrieve token's output values rather than the whole vocabulary
the threshold is set externally, by a person, not learned
lowering it makes the system retrieve more often

answers.answer: A thought is an action in language space that does not affect the external environment, so it produces no observation feedback. Every other action reaches something outside the model and returns an observation. The only thing a thought changes is the model's own context, and that context is what the next step reads, so a thought informs the next action without the environment ever seeing it.
accept: a thought does not affect the external environment
a thought produces no observation feedback, while a real action returns an observation
it changes only the model's context, which the next step reads

answers.answer: Self-RAG decides whether to retrieve at all for the next output segment, per step, conditioned on the input and everything generated so far; when the answer is no it just continues as a standard language model. ReAct decides what to retrieve next, using reasoning over the previous observation to target the following query against the external source.
accept: Self-RAG decides whether retrieval is needed for the next segment
ReAct decides what to retrieve next
ReAct's next query is chosen from the previous observation by the model's reasoning

answers.answer: Act is the same method with one half removed, so the difference is attributable to the reasoning rather than to any of the other differences between two unrelated systems. ALFWorld shows a large gap, 71 percent for the best ReAct trial against 45 percent for the best Act trial. WebShop shows the other case: acting alone already performed on par with the IL and IL+RL methods, and reasoning added an absolute 10 percent on top. Quoting only ALFWorld would suggest the reasoning half carries the whole result.
accept: the ablation isolates one half, so the difference is attributable to it
ALFWorld: 71 percent for ReAct against 45 percent for Act
on WebShop acting alone already matched the prior methods
reasoning added about 10 percent absolute there, so the size of the ablation's effect varies by benchmark
